blocks.text: Cardiovascular disease (CVD) prevention is a coordinated set of actions, at the population level or targeted at an individual at risk of developing cardiovascular disease, that are aimed at eliminating or minimizing the impact of CVDs and their related disabilities.

blocks.text: Table 20.1: Cardiovascular Disease Risk Classification and WHO Risk estimation
Subjects with any of the following:
Documented Cardiovascular Disease (clinical or unequivocal on imaging), including:
Coronary revascularization or other arterial revascularization procedures
Unequivocal imaging evidence of CVD (e.g., plaque on coronary angiography or carotid ultrasound). Does not include increased carotid intima-media thickness alone.

blocks.text: Diabetes Mellitus with target organ damage (e.g., proteinuria) or major risk factors such as smoking, marked hypercholesterolemia, or marked hypertension.
Severe Chronic Kidney Disease (GFR <30 mL/min/1.73 m²).
Cholesterol >8 mmol/L (>310 mg/dL), e.g., familial hypercholesterolemia
Most other patients with Diabetes Mellitus (except young people with type 1 DM without major risk factors).
Moderate Chronic Kidney Disease (GFR 30–59 mL/min/1.73 m²).
Calculated CVD risk score ≥1% and <5% over 10 years.
Many middle-aged individuals fall into this category.
Table 20.2: General measures for Lifestyle modification
No exposure to tobacco in any form.
Reduce dietary sodium intake to ≤2.4 g sodium/day (≈6 g sodium chloride/day).
Emphasize whole grains, vegetables, fruits, and fish.
Alcohol consumption should not exceed 5 days/week.
1 unit of alcohol = 25 mL spirits, 125 mL wine, 340 mL beer/sorghum beer, or 60 mL sherry.
At least 150 minutes/week of moderate-intensity aerobic exercise (e.g., 30 minutes/day for 5 days/week), OR
75 minutes/week of vigorous-intensity aerobic exercise (e.g., 15 minutes/day for 5 days/week), OR
An equivalent combination of moderate and vigorous activity.
Very high risk: <1.8 mmol/L (<70 mg/dL) or ≥50% reduction if baseline is 1.8–3.5 mmol/L.
High risk:<2.6 mmol/L (<100 mg/dL) or ≥50% reduction if baseline is 2.6–5.1 mmol/L.
Higher levels warrant assessment of other risk factors.
Recommended to repeat CV risk assessment every 5years, and more often for individuals with risks close to thresholds mandating treatment.
